$comment: The Phase 4 recovery manifest. One file, machine-readable, so Phase 4 can execute it without
another investigation. Every entry says what is wrong, whether it can be recovered, from where,
by which operation, and the check that proves the repair worked.
Reconciled 2026-10-12 against the live primary. Every figure below was re-measured, not carried
forward; where a count moves with the data the query that produced it is given, so Phase 4 can
re-measure rather than trust this file. Three entries changed classification on this pass and the
reasons are recorded in each: the PK OHLC anomaly is the exchange's own closing convention and not
a defect, the US one is floating-point noise, and a genuinely independent second provider for PSX
was found, which the previous revision stated did not exist.
Classification, and the distinction matters more than the counts:
real_observation  - the data is correct and must never be 'repaired'
by_design         - a deliberate limit of the collector, documented, not a fault
listing_limit     - the instrument did not exist earlier; nothing is missing
source_defect     - the provider sent it this way; recovery depends on the provider
recoverable_gap   - genuinely missing and obtainable from a source we already use
blocked           - cannot be resolved inside this repository
measured_against: Supabase primary, PriceSnapshot 831,027 rows / 614 assets / 317 MB database

entries.source: Pakistan Stock Exchange daily closing file

measured.comparison: US 251-253/yr and FX 257-262/yr over the same span
measured.re_measured_2026_10_12: identical to the previous revision; the shape has not moved

why: jobs/psx.py DEEP_DAYS = 820 fetches a dense daily stretch of about 2.25 years, sized to
jobs/horizons.py's LONG_RANGE + 40 = 540 sessions. Behind it the job stores a monthly grid
of RISING_MONTHS = 24 anchors, which is the 12-13 rows a year seen for 2019-2023.
So this is the collector's designed shape, not a failed fetch.

what_the_sparse_grid_actually_supports.$note: Required by the Phase 1 brief: say which computations the grid serves and which need dense daily history. Measured 2026-10-12 over the 176 active PK names.
served_by_the_monthly_grid: The 24-month relative return (nbt.RISING_MONTHS = 24), which reads monthly anchors by construction.
The price history chart, which plots anchors over the long span.
served_by_the_dense_2024-onward_stretch_: jobs/horizons.py's longer read in full: LONG_SLOW = 200, LONG_RANGE = 500, MIN_LONG = 220.
155 of 176 active names clear 540 sessions from 2024-01-01 alone; 158 clear it over all stored history and 167 clear the 220 minimum.
The deepest name holds 559 dense sessions against the 540 target, so the margin is 19 sessions and DEEP_DAYS has no slack to lose.
would_require_dense_pre_2024_daily: Any historical evaluation or backtest spanning more than about 2.25 years. That consumer does not exist yet; it is Phase 3's 'historical evaluation'.
Until it does, nothing downstream reads a pre-2024 PK daily close, and nothing silently substitutes a monthly anchor for one.
what_the_sparse_grid_actually_supports.conclusion: Not complete, and not to be marked complete. The gap is real but binds only on work Phase 3 has yet to build, which is why it stays a Phase 4 item rather than a current-phase blocker.

entries.impact: Long-horizon PSX historical evaluation before 2024 rests on monthly anchors, not daily closes. Current verdicts are unaffected: they read recent windows that fall inside the dense stretch.
entries.proposed_source: Either of two, and they are independent of each other.

proposed_sources.source: The exchange's own archive, which jobs/psx.py already knows: ARCHIVE_FROM = 2013-11-04.
proposed_sources.pros: Raw as-traded closes in exactly the shape already stored. No semantic conversion.
proposed_sources.cons: Same restricted upstream as psx-redistribution-licence below. Host began refusing at roughly 600 requests in one session.

proposed_sources.source: Yahoo Finance, symbol + '.KA' (exchange KAR, currency PKR). Reached through the same yfinance path jobs/prices.py already uses for US, FX and commodities.

verified_2026_10_12.coverage: 156 of the 176 active PSX names resolve; 20 return HTTP 404 (BBFL, BFBIO, BML, ENGROH, GAL, GCWL, GDL, ITANZ, LSEVL, QTECH, SELECT, SOYASUP, SPAC1, SPSL, STL, TISL, WAFI, WAHDAT, ZAL, ZUMA), most of them recent listings.
verified_2026_10_12.depth: firstTradeDate 2008-01-01; bars present from 2018-01-01, which covers the whole 2019-2023 gap.
verified_2026_10_12.density_after_filtering: 245/251/246/248/244 real sessions for 2019-2023 against the 12-13 stored now, and against PSX's true ~248.
verified_2026_10_12.agreement: 4,524 overlapping bars compared against the stored exchange file: 96.1% of closes identical to within 0.01% and 99.5% of volumes exact. The session calendar agrees exactly - no session in one and absent from the other.
verified_2026_10_12.fidelity_conclusion: This is the same market data, not an approximation.

two_defects_that_must_be_handled_and_bot.defect: Synthetic flat bars. Yahoo fills a session it does not have with open=high=low=close and volume 0 rather than omitting it. Measured: 16/11/15/12/16 such bars per year for 2019-2023, and they fall on Pakistan's public holidays (Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha, Ashura, Kashmir Day, Pakistan Day, Independence Day). The same mechanism produced a fabricated bar on 2026-10-08, a real trading session Yahoo missed, for all 156 names - 86 of those closes were more than 1% from the true close.
two_defects_that_must_be_handled_and_bot.filter: Reject any bar where volume = 0 AND open = high = low = close. This removes holiday padding and missed-session padding together, and no real PSX session is lost by it: a genuine zero-volume session does not also have four equal prices that differ from the previous close.

two_defects_that_must_be_handled_and_bot.defect: Corporate-action semantics differ. Yahoo returns a split/bonus-adjusted series; the exchange file stores raw as-traded prices. Measured on three names whose ratio is constant backwards from the event date: BPL 0.8333 (5/6, a 20% bonus), CLOV 0.8696 (20/23), BAPL 0.6094. Every other name agreed exactly, so this is confined to names with a corporate action inside the window.
two_defects_that_must_be_handled_and_bot.filter: Never mix the two series for one asset. Either store Yahoo bars under their own source and keep them separate, or re-base them onto the stored raw series at the latest common date. Appending adjusted history to raw history would create a price jump that never happened.

proposed_sources.pros: A genuinely independent upstream - not a scraper of dps.psx.com.pk - reached through a provider path and a licence posture this project has already accepted for every other asset class.
proposed_sources.cons: 88.6% coverage, not 100%. Adjusted rather than raw. Fabricates bars it does not have. See psx-redistribution-licence: this changes which provider's terms apply, it does not grant redistribution rights.

entries.recovery_operation: Raise DEEP_DAYS, or run a dated backfill over 2019-01-01..2024-06-30 through the existing psx.py path, which is idempotent and never deletes. If the Yahoo route is used instead, apply both filters above and store under a distinct source so the two series can always be told apart. Respect the measured request ceiling on the exchange host: refusals began at roughly 600 requests in one session.
entries.integrity_check: Stored distinct PK session dates per year reaches 240+ for each of 2019-2023; no existing row's close changes; and no stored bar has volume = 0 with four equal prices.
entries.blocked_by: psx-redistribution-licence - recovering more PSX history does not change the permission question below.

entries.$reclassified: Was part of 'ohlc-close-outside-own-range' and classified source_defect. Re-measured 2026-10-12 and it is not a defect. Split out because the three markets in that entry turned out to have three unrelated causes.

measured.close_equals_previous_session_close: 1133 of the 1231 rows that have a previous session (92.0%)

why: PSX sets a scrip's official closing price from the closing window, and where a name did not
trade enough in that window the exchange carries the previous close forward. The high and low
are the day's actual traded extremes, so a carried-forward close can sit outside them.
That is the exchange's published closing-price convention, not a corrupt value: 92% of these
rows have a close exactly equal to the previous session's close, and 97% are thin-volume names.
Query that shows it: compare close against lag(close) OVER (PARTITION BY assetId ORDER BY date).
correction_to_the_previous_revision: That revision said 'the trade grader already reads these bars as unavailable rather than
trusting them'. No code does that. Nothing in jobs/, lib/ or tools/ tests close against high
and low; tools/trade_sim.py loads open, high, low and close unfiltered. The claim described a
It does not need to exist. High and low are the real traded extremes, so target and stop
detection is correct as it stands, and the close is the exchange's official close. Discarding
these 1,232 bars as 'unavailable' would have thrown away valid observations.
entries.impact: None. These are correct records of what the exchange published.
entries.recovery_operation: NONE. Do not 'repair' these rows and do not add a validator that rejects a close outside its own high/low for PK - it would discard 1,232 valid exchange closes.
entries.integrity_check: The 1,133 rows whose close equals the previous session's close still read that way after any Phase 4 pass.
entries.residue: 98 rows do not match the previous close and have no explanation yet. Small enough to inspect one by one rather than reason about in aggregate; left for Phase 4 to look at directly.
entries.query: SELECT count(*) FROM "PriceSnapshot" s JOIN "Asset" a ON a.id=s."assetId" JOIN "Industry" i ON i.id=a."industryId" WHERE i.market='PK' AND (s.close > s.high OR s.close < s.low)

entries.$reclassified: Was part of 'ohlc-close-outside-own-range'. Kept as a defect - it is the only one of the three that is one - and separated because its cause is specific to FX and is worth stating.

measured.close_equals_previous_session_close: 137 of 4142 (3.3%), so the PK explanation does not apply here
measured.worked_example: USDPKR 2026-10-09: high 268.235, low 267.412, close 276.75 - the close is 3.2% above the day's high, and the same 276.75 appears on 2026-10-07 and a near-identical 276.70 on 2026-10-08.

why: The close is not drawn from the same venue as the OHLC. The OHLC sits around the interbank
rate while the close sits around a different quote - for USDPKR, roughly the open-market rate.
A repeated, flat close against a moving intraday range is what that looks like.
This is a genuine provider inconsistency, and unlike the PK case there is no convention that
entries.impact: 27 FX names, USDPKR among them. Any calculation that mixes the close with the same bar's high or low is comparing two venues. The PKR rate matters to PSX-facing analysis, so this is the FX row to look at first.
entries.proposed_source: Re-fetch the affected dates from the same provider and keep the new bar only when it is internally consistent. No independent second FX provider has been evaluated - unlike the PK case, where one now exists.
entries.recovery_operation: Per affected (assetId, date), re-fetch and upsert only if high >= low AND low <= close <= high. Never edit a stored value in place.
entries.integrity_check: Count of FX rows where close > high OR close < low falls, and no row count decreases.
entries.query: SELECT count(*) FROM "PriceSnapshot" s JOIN "Asset" a ON a.id=s."assetId" JOIN "Industry" i ON i.id=a."industryId" WHERE i.market='FX' AND (s.close > s.high OR s.close < s.low)

entries.$reclassified: Was part of 'ohlc-close-outside-own-range'. It is floating-point noise, not a defect, and recording it as one invited a repair that would have been a no-op at best.

measured.example: AGNC 2023-03-20: low 5.71911239624024, close 5.71911239624023 - a difference of 1 in the 15th significant digit.

entries.why: The close equals the high or the low to within one unit in the last place of a double. The comparison is true; the discrepancy is not. These bars are correct.
entries.impact: None at any precision anyone trades or displays at.
entries.recovery_operation: NONE. If a future validator flags these, give it a tolerance of one ULP rather than re-fetching 49 correct bars.

entries.why: The WTI front-month settled below zero on 20 April 2020. A futures close under zero is an observation.
entries.impact: None. Any validator that treats close <= 0 as malformed is wrong for futures.
entries.recovery_operation: NONE. Do not change this value. Do not let a cleanup pass 'fix' it.
entries.integrity_check: The row still reads -37.63 after any Phase 4 pass.

entries.why: The exchange published its own Saturday file. Stored as received; every decision reader skips weekend rows for a weekday market (jobs/sessions.py session_bar, rule 95).
entries.impact: None on verdicts. It inflates PK row counts by 171.
entries.recovery_operation: Optional. Leaving it is honest - it is what the exchange published. Removing it would delete a real record of a real file.
entries.integrity_check: If removed, PK rows fall by exactly 171 and no other date is touched.

entries.why: These instruments were listed after the universe floor. Nothing is missing; the history does not exist.
entries.impact: Rules needing a long window decline to read them, which is correct behaviour and already reported as 'incomplete' rather than guessed.
entries.recovery_operation: NONE. Do not pad a history that never existed.
entries.integrity_check: Each asset's first stored date equals the provider's earliest available date for it.

cof_verified_2026-10-12.verdict: Still recovered, unchanged since the previous revision. COF is not a late listing and is not in this entry's scope.
cof_verified_2026-10-12.tool: tools/recover_asset.py - one asset, upsert only, never is_full, and it re-reads every pre-existing bar afterwards and fails the run if one was lost or altered. Idempotent and safe to re-run.

entries.note: 17 of the 20 PSX names Yahoo does not carry are in or near this group, which is consistent: a provider that has not listed a symbol and an exchange that listed it last quarter are the same fact seen twice.

measured.measured_against: distinct stored PK weekday session dates, which are themselves sparse before 2024 - see psx-pre-2024-monthly-grid

entries.why: A name absent from a daily closing file it should appear in: either it did not trade that session, or the file was not fetched. The two are not distinguishable from stored data alone.
entries.new_2026-10-12: They are now distinguishable from outside it. Yahoo .KA covers 156 of the 176 names independently, and over the 29-session window measured on 2026-09-01..2026-10-09 the two sources' session calendars agreed exactly. Checking a suspected missing session against Yahoo separates 'did not trade' from 'was not fetched' without another investigation.
entries.impact: PSX per-asset windows are shorter than the session count suggests. Bounded by the same pre-2024 sparsity above.
entries.proposed_source: The same PSX daily closing files, re-fetched for the specific missing dates; Yahoo .KA as the cross-check that says which dates are worth re-fetching.
entries.recovery_operation: Resolve psx-pre-2024-monthly-grid first; re-measure afterwards, because most of these gaps are that entry seen per asset.
entries.integrity_check: Re-run the span query; missing_sessions_inside_span falls for each named symbol and no bar is lost.

entries.scope: PK market data distribution only. No other asset class is affected.
why: PSX's own legal notice prohibits 'any dissemination, transmission, sale, and commercial use
of Market Data feed' without a licence from PSX, including on a delayed basis. Its terms of
use permit 'a single, unaltered, permanent copy' for 'personal, non-commercial use only'.
This product republishes PSX closes publicly on /psx for 176 names.

evaluation_2026-10-12.$note: A second, bounded evaluation. The previous one concluded every route was the same dps.psx.com.pk upstream. That conclusion was right about the routes it checked and wrong to stop there: one independent provider does carry PSX.

candidates.result: Works. HTTP 200, 22,561 bytes for 2026-10-09. Raw as-traded OHLCV, archive back to 2013-11-04.
candidates.reason: It is the restricted feed itself. Nothing about continuing to use it changes the permission question.

candidates.result: Does not resolve. Connection fails at the network level (curl exit, HTTP 000). Re-checked 2026-10-12, same as the previous evaluation.

CORRECTION to the previous evaluation, which recorded this as a 404. It is not dead: it answers 200 when called with browser headers from the company page that uses it, and 404 to a bare request. Confirmed by loading dps.psx.com.pk/company/OGDC in a browser and reading its network traffic.
candidates.reason: What it returns is intraday tick data for the current session - [timestamp, price, size] triples - not EOD OHLCV and no history. And it is the same restricted upstream, so even complete data from it would not change the permission question.

candidates.result: Qualifies as an independent source. 156/176 names, dense daily from 2018-01-01, 96.1% of closes and 99.5% of volumes identical to the stored exchange file over 4,524 compared bars, session calendars in exact agreement. Full detail and its two defects are under psx-pre-2024-monthly-grid.
candidates.qualifies: as a secondary and as a recovery source, not as a replacement
candidates.reason: 88.6% coverage, adjusted rather than raw prices, and it fabricates flat zero-volume bars for sessions it is missing. A replacement has to be complete and raw; a cross-check and a history source do not.

candidates.result: Lists the full PSX symbol universe - the free /stocks?country=Pakistan endpoint returns it without a key. Time series needs an API key, which needs an account.
candidates.reason: No account was created, so whether the free tier actually serves PSX time series is unverified. Left for the owner to decide; it is the one remaining candidate that could be checked cheaply.

candidates.result: Disqualified on access policy, not capability. robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /' with allowances only for Bingbot and Googlebot, and the site serves an active proof-of-work browser challenge.
candidates.reason: Collecting from it would mean defeating a bot check against an explicit disallow. Out of bounds regardless of what the data looks like.

what_this_changes_and_what_it_does_not: CHANGES: the previous revision said of the malformed-bar entry that 'there is no second
provider for these instruments'. For PK that is now false. An independent provider exists,
it agrees with the exchange file to 96.1%, and it reaches back to 2018 - which makes the
pre-2024 history recoverable without the exchange archive, and makes missing PSX sessions
DOES NOT CHANGE: the redistribution question. Yahoo's own terms restrict redistribution too.
Switching provider does not obtain a licence; it changes whose terms govern the PK surface,
from an exchange whose notice names delayed redistribution explicitly to a provider this
project already relies on, and already republishes, for US, FX and commodity data.
That is a real difference in the owner's risk posture and it is not a legal opinion.
Nobody in this repository can give one.

entries.impact: The public PSX surface republishes this data. Collection and private use are unaffected.
entries.recovery_operation: Not a data operation. The owner chooses: restrict the PSX surface to non-public use, obtain a licence, move the public PK surface onto the Yahoo series and accept that provider's terms instead, or accept the current risk explicitly.
